target: Nothing is absent. The capsules were missing from the specimens, so the record should be dropped. 'densely papillose' probably describes the perianth (PO:0009058, papillose FLOPO:0991059), not the fruit (PO:0009001).

target: No leaf is absent. The flowering stems (PO:0009047) look leafless because the cauline leaves (PO:0000013) are few and small. The basal leaves are pinnatipartite (FLOPO:0991156).

target: Only the leaves in the lower 1/3 to 1/2 of the leafy shoot have no blade (they are just sheaths, PO:0020104). The upper leaves have a pubescent lamina (PO:0020039).
fix: 'bladeless in basal X', 'bladeless sheaths' and 'lower leaves bladeless' apply only to the leaves at that position. Keep the position as context and never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.

target: The outer female florets (pistillate flower PO:0025599) have no pappus. The inner bisexual florets (flower PO:0009046) have a pappus (PO:0025393) of white hairs.

reason: In Ifloga the female florets lack a pappus and the bisexual florets have one.

target: aril (PO:0009090) absent (PATO:0000462). The seed (PO:0009010) is present and mottled.
fix: 'aril absent', 'exarillate' and 'without aril' map to aril (PO:0009090) absent and never to seed absent. The part that is absent is the noun the word 'absent' modifies.

target: Only the sheathing cauline leaves (PO:0000013, sheathing FLOPO:0991105) are absent. The basal leaves are present.
fix: 'without <modifier> leaves' (sheathing, cauline, stem, floating) denies only that kind of leaf. Keep the modifier as bearer or context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.

target: Keep bracteole (PO:0009043) absent, at least in the female flowers. 'beige or pinkish-fawn' describes another part, probably the female spike, perhaps the stigmas or hairs. It does not describe the bracteoles.
fix: A colour phrase with no noun of its own belongs to the subject of its clause. Never attach it to a part that the same clause or a nearby one calls absent.
reason: Typha latifolia is known for lacking bracteoles in its female flowers, so a colour on the bracteoles is a misattribution.

target: No leaf absence. The branches (PO:0025073) and the axis below the peduncles have no leaves along most of their length, and the leaves sit near the tips. The leaves exist and are tinged pink.
fix: '<axis> leafless', 'leafless up to X' and 'leafless like the branches' describe where on an axis the leaves sit. Record it on the axis or drop it. Never record a plant-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: The leaves are described as pink, so the statement is only about the bare part of the axis.

target: The sterile florets (Chusquea's 'glumes' III and IV, which are sterile lemmas) have no real palea. The fertile floret's palea (PO:0009038) is coriaceous.
fix: 'without (significant) palea' near sterile lemmas or reduced florets applies to those florets only. Keep 'sterile floret' as context. 'without significant X' means reduced or minute, not absent.
reason: Chusquea has one fertile floret with a palea, which is the one described.

target: The male spikelets (staminate) have no glumes (PO:0009039). The female spikelets have glumes, and their lower glume (PO:0006002) has an acuminate apex.
fix: 'Male spikelet glumes absent' and 'glumes absent in male spikelets' carry the spikelet's sex. Keep 'staminate spikelet' as context and never record a taxon-wide 'glume absent'.

target: The lower glume (PO:0006002) has no lateral veins, so it has one vein. Record the absence on the veins, with 'lateral' as context, not on the glume.
fix: In KEW-style '<part> <subpart> absent' entries, the absent thing is the last noun before 'absent' (veins, keels, hairs, awns). Its bearer is the first noun.
reason: The glumes are described as persistent, so they exist.

target: The glume (PO:0009039) is not keeled. Negate the closest available term (keel-shaped PATO:0002522) or drop the statement. The glume is present.
fix: 'without keel(s)' and 'ecarinate' deny a keel on the part. Read them as 'not keeled' on that part, never as the part being absent. Do not use PO:0025327 keel, which is the keel of a legume flower.
reason: The glume's length is described, so it exists.

target: The lemma (PO:0009037) is not keeled. Negate keel-shaped (PATO:0002522) or drop the statement. The lemma is present and membranous.

target: The leaf (PO:0025034) is glabrous (PATO:0000453): hairs (trichome PO:0000282) are absent from the leaf.
fix: In tables written as 'Character: value', such as 'Hairs: absent' or 'Stomata: present', the absent or present thing is the character name. The section's organ is only its bearer.
reason: This is a leaf anatomy table. Its entries 'Hairs: absent' and 'Stomata: present' are about the hairs and the stomata, not the leaf.

target: The stem has no leaves: cauline leaf (PO:0000013) absent, or the stem is scapiform (FLOPO:0991224). The basal leaves are long and narrow.

target: Only the allomorphic female flowers (pistillate flower PO:0025599, with 'allomorphic' as context) are absent. Normal female and male flowers are present.

target: The annulus (the ring at the mouth of the perianth tube) is absent. Its bearer is the perianth (PO:0009058), not the corolla. 'limb brown' also belongs on the perianth.
fix: In Aristolochia, 'annulus absent' and 'syrinx absent' deny a structure of the perianth tube. Record the structure as the absent thing. In Aristolochiaceae, words about the perianth (limb, tube, utricle) map to perianth, not corolla.
reason: Aristolochia has a perianth with no corolla, and the annulus is part of it.

target: The syrinx (a structure at the mouth of the perianth tube) is absent. Its bearer is the perianth (PO:0009058). 'lobe ovate' also belongs on the perianth lobe.
fix: Same rule as X02087.

target: Colleters (FLOPO_0986023) on the leaf lamina (PO:0020039) are absent. The lamina is present and filiform.
fix: '<location> colleters absent', 'laminar glands absent' and similar deny the small structures on the part. The location word gives only the bearer.

target: Only the basal sheaths (leaf sheath PO:0020104, with 'basal' as context) have no blade. The blades of the other leaves are flat.

reason: Carex usually has bladeless basal sheaths and flat-bladed leaves above them.

target: Short shoots (PO:0004701, tufts of leaves in the leaf axils, 'axillary' as context) are absent. The leaves are present and not marcescent.

target: Probably one set of involucre teeth (or the tepals) lacks awns while another set has straight awns. The text given does not show which.

target: The rosette or stem has no axillary vegetative branches. The twisted branches belong to the inflorescence.

target: Only the basal spikelets (spikelet PO:0009051, with 'basal' as context) are absent. The terminal spikelet is present and ovoid or ellipsoid.

target: Only the caudex (the woody stem base) is absent. Record it with 'caudex' as the bearer or context. The aerial stems (PO:0009047) are present and slender.

target: cauline leaf (PO:0000013) absent. The basal leaves are present and sessile.
fix: 'cauline leaves absent' maps to cauline leaf (PO:0000013) absent. Never drop the word 'cauline'.

target: The seed (PO:0009010) has no recurved flap over the hilum (PO:0020063). Drop the absence or record it with 'flap over hilum' as context. The seed is present and tan.
fix: '<structure> over/on <part> absent' denies the structure, not the part. If the structure has no term, drop the absence instead of moving it to the organ.
reason: The seed is described as tan, so it exists.

target: Only the outer staminodes (sterile stamens) have no anthers. The fertile stamens have anthers (PO:0009066). 'epidermis smooth' probably describes the seed coat (PO:0009088), not the anther.
